# `silk/mem/box`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

One owned value on the heap, for recursive data and for values that must have a fixed-size
handle.

## When to use
Use [`Box`](#Box) when a type must contain itself, such as a tree node that owns child nodes. A field
of type `Box<Node>` has a fixed size, so the compiler can lay out `Node`. Use [`make`](#Box.impl.make) to
allocate, [`get`](#Box.impl.get) or [`getMut`](#Box.impl.getMut) to borrow the value, and [`into`](#Box.impl.into) to get the value back.

## Details
A box owns one allocation and one value. [`get`](#Box.impl.get) and [`getMut`](#Box.impl.getMut) return a slice of length 1,
because a Silk function cannot return a bare borrowed value. Dropping a box drops its value and
releases the allocation. [`into`](#Box.impl.into) moves the value out and releases the allocation one time.

## Gotchas
Dropping a chain of boxes uses one stack frame for each link. For a very long chain, take the
links apart with [`into`](#Box.impl.into) in a loop.

## Examples
### Store and recover one owned value
```silk
import silk.mem.box { Box }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut boxed = run Box<i32>.make(40) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut slot = Box<i32>.getMut(&mut boxed)
  slot[0] = slot[0] + 2
  drop slot
  let value = Box<i32>.into(move boxed)
  if value != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Box` with `import silk.mem.box { Box }`.

<a id="Box"></a>

## `Box`

```silk
pub struct Box<T>
```

An owner of one heap-allocated value of type `T`.

### When to use

Use a box when a type must contain itself, such as a tree node that owns child nodes. A field
of type `Box<Node>` has a fixed size, so the compiler can lay out `Node`. Use [`make`](#Box.impl.make) to
allocate, [`get`](#Box.impl.get) or [`getMut`](#Box.impl.getMut) to borrow the value, and [`into`](#Box.impl.into) to get the value back.

### Details

The size of `Box<T>` does not depend on `T`, so a type can contain a box of itself. Dropping a
box drops the value and then releases the allocation. A box is affine. It is not `Copy`.

### Gotchas

Dropping a chain of boxes uses one stack frame for each link. For a very long chain, take the
links apart with [`into`](#Box.impl.into) in a loop.

<a id="Box.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn make<'env>(value: T) -> Box<T> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Allocates space for one `T`, moves `value` into it, and returns the box.

#### Details

The allocation comes from the active `Allocator`. The box owns the value and the allocation.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the memory. No box is made, and `value`
  is dropped.

<a id="Box.impl.get"></a>

### Method `get`

```silk
pub fn get(self: &Self) -> &[T]
```

Returns a shared borrow of the value, as a slice of length 1.

#### Details

Read the value as `slice[0]`. The slice borrows the box. The box cannot change or move while
the slice is live.

<a id="Box.impl.getMut"></a>

### Method `getMut`

```silk
pub fn getMut(self: &mut Self) -> &mut [T]
```

Returns an exclusive borrow of the value, as a slice of length 1.

#### Details

Change the value through `slice[0]`. The slice borrows the box exclusively. No other use of
the box is possible while the slice is live. Drop the slice to end the borrow early.

<a id="Box.impl.into"></a>

### Method `into`

```silk
pub fn into(self: Self) -> T
```

Moves the value out of the box, releases the allocation, and returns the value.

#### When to use

Use `into` when the caller needs the value itself, not a borrow. Use it in a loop to take
apart a long chain of boxes without deep recursion. A plain drop of such a chain uses one
stack frame for each link.
